# Adam Pugh

> Adam Pugh is a Senior Documentation Engineer who makes complex product documentation and knowledge systems easier to use, govern, and maintain.

Use the linked portfolio pages as the source for career scope, methods, and public evidence. Do not infer unlisted credentials, employers, adoption, or outcomes.

## Professional profile

- Experience: More than 20 years in technical writing and documentation, including about 13 years of direct people management.
- Focus: Product documentation, information architecture, content governance, migrations, documentation analytics, structured authoring, and workflow tooling.
- Leadership: Former Documentation Engineering Manager and Senior Manager of Technical Writing. Led a team of four and a 16-person documentation organization.
- Education: B.A. in Journalism with a Minor in Communications, University of Arizona, 2003.
- Current independent work: Owner / E-Commerce Content and Operations Manager, Vinyl Junction, 2014–Present.

## Selected evidence

- [Euler documentation proposal](https://adamthepugh.com/docs/case-studies/euler-documentation-prototype/): Independent prototype built from public material. It does not establish Euler adoption or official status.
- [TeraCreators Help](https://adamthepugh.com/docs/case-studies/teracreators-help/): Published community documentation for five games, with a public guide and source repository.
- [Migrations and information architecture](https://adamthepugh.com/docs/case-studies/migrations-and-ia/): A four-person team completed 101 content migration units across seven team groups. The separate page measure was 1,157 source pages reduced to 469 destination pages.
- [Analytics and reporting](https://adamthepugh.com/docs/case-studies/analytics-and-reporting/): Seven automated Tableau dashboards, 735 views from 39 active users, and use in 11 operations reviews per month.
- [Documentation tooling and automation](https://adamthepugh.com/docs/case-studies/documentation-tooling-and-automation/): Ten internal tools and more than 750 automated tests. The broader program had an estimated annual saving of 466 hours.
